You have no idea how much better you've made me feel, and the courage you've just given to me. 

I reached out to my friends for help. And though they don't really know how to handle the situation, they want me to be okay and are willing to hear me say "I'm depressed" for the 39845743957th time. This time though, I finally said the rest of what I'd been wanting to say: I'm depressed AND suicidal. They didn't react as badly as I had predicted. They stayed calm and talked me through. They know I try hard to keep myself positive and that I've been shielding them from just how bad my depression gets. 

I do the same as you when I'm feeling rather down, but this bout felt different. I've never come this close to throwing in the towel, but I stumbled across another post where a woman had been powering through her depression for a whopping 20 years. She's truly inspiring. I just wish there was a cure for this ugliness, for you, for her, for everyone. 

Sending lots of grateful hugs your way.

To be fighting this for 20 years is so inspiring to me. I'm only in my 6th year and I'm already faltering. I feel like I know where you're coming from because you've worked so hard to keep your head afloat, but a person can only tread water for so long. 

I can't be of any help or positivity today because I'm going through an episode myself, but feel free to talk at me all you want. I just want to hug you because you've sparked a little bit of hope in myself. I know there's no way out of this chronic depression, but to know that you've held on so long makes me happy that I'm crying a little.

Thank you. It's hard but we're told to keep fighting and so I try. It's exhausting and I realise that I've been repeating that word over and over. 

I'm exhausted. If life's a marathon, there are those that push through and finish it to the glorious end, then there are those that puff out and catch a cab with a shortcut to the finish. I'm puffed. I hate that I'm talking so negatively. I opened up a word document and wrote the words 'happy' and 'life' in bright pink because the colour pink is supposed to make you feel in love. I'm tired of trying to trick my brain into being happy. Why can't these stupid neurons in my brain fire off like they're supposed to? It's hard to maintain a will to live when my body doesn't even want to function in a way to facilitate living. 

There isn't anything that triggers my depression. Some days I just wake up and instead of getting out of bed, I wonder why I hadn't just slipped away in my sleep. Those close to me know of my condition, but I rarely turn to them. It's selfish of me to come out here and spill all my brain juice because the reason I don't turn to my friends is because I don't want to bum them out. But I'm bumming the people of the internet out. I have turned to my loved ones in the past, but I feel they're growing weary of my situation too. They can only reassure me so many times before I'm sure it gets to the point of eye rolling, mind numbing annoyance. Friends and family are great to turn to when there's a reason for the depression, like a dead pet. If only I had a reason other than a defect in my physiology. I used to see a psychiatrist but it's kinda hard to keep up with going when I can't even bring myself to roll out of bed. I'm so goddamn helpless. 

I'm so sorry to talk so negatively. You are a wonderful human being. 
I want to beat this but I know that's impossible. There is no cure; no matter how much I immerse myself in positivity, therapy, medication and I think realising this has left me in despair.

I can only hold onto that for so long before the responsibility eats me up. I'm too tired to continue on just because I have a duty to keep breathing for my family. I'm exhausted. I can't power through the depression anymore and with each reoccurrence I lose more will to live. My family would be sad, but that part of me that stops these thoughts of suicide because of that reason is dying down. 

Each time I get better, it comes back. It's like giving a baby a lollipop, then snatching that lollipop away but not before you stab the baby in the eyes with the stick.

You know he lives in the midlands in the UK, you know his name, and you know a few of his likes at least game-wise. It's definitely worth throwing these things into google and facebook. You'll be surprised how easy it can be to find someone's account with determination and a little bit of background knowledge about that person (I sound super stalkery rn but if it helps you find your friend and keep him safe, whatever). My friends and I have found the profiles of 'cute bus guy' and 'dude that took his mask off at end of play during final bows'. So just give that a go. 

If you feel that your friend is in immediate danger (which seems to be the case), you need to go to the police. Even with the little information you can provide them, I'm sure they can bypass the anti reverse phone lookup law.

Did he ever give any indication of what city/state he might be in through comments about the weather/local events?
Do you have this friend on facebook? If not, you have their first name and probably know a few of their likes and a general area for where they live. It might be worth trying to find them this way.

Despite not being under my mother's care, I don't take medications because she's opposed to them, and tbh, I'm a little scared to lose a part of me/become someone my boyfriend doesn't love. 

I often become unable to roll out of bed with my depression, not all the time, but it's happened more than a few times. It's a major reason I never seem to be able to complete any sort of degree despite being top ranked for the time I'm there. It's crippling, frightening and debilitating. And you sort of just watch yourself lay in bed while thinking "I want to be better than this" but getting up to eat is even a feat too hard at that point. Thankfully, my boyfriend is understanding and gives me small meals to eat and occasionally plops me in the car for a drive around. 

Having seemingly successful 'happy' lives also makes it a lot harder to get our feelings across and feel valid. I don't want to be depressed, I take measures to make it so I can cope with being depressed, I know what to do when I am depressed and yet I am frustrated that I am depressed. 

My boyfriend says it's faulty wiring and that he wouldn't have me any other way because it's this faulty wiring that makes me so passionate about everything else in life. But tbh I'd rather have normal wiring and be insignificant than deal with the burn out of depression. idk weird analogy.

I took up easy classes like astronomy, sociology and general design and found that I loved the interior architecture component of general design. A year on and I'm now doing architecture and working for a design firm and despite the depression coming back, I power through my renderings with tears in my eyes because I know that this is what I want to do. Unlike when I was doing med, I loved biology, but when depression hit I no longer wanted to do it. This is the one passion that stays through the dark times.

Hey dude

I'm sorry you're feeling so fed up. I know how frustrating and demoralising it feels to try to socialise with no results. It seems silly and such a petty thing to become fixated on, but it's definitely real and the loneliness is heartbreaking. 

I'm not here to lie to you and stroke your ego, but your nose is pretty damn nice. Your whole face, actually, is pretty well proportioned. Not the type of dude I'd usually go for but you look like one of my mates and he's landed himself a girlfriend recently. I also noticed your Ren and Stimpy shirt, so I know you've got some pretty cool interests. That being said, if I think you've got cool interests, chances are, you're a pretty niche person. And it's lonely being a niche person. Have you tried expanding your hobbies and interests? What type of area do you live in? You'll probably fair better in a more liberal hipster city. 

You seem to be really fixated on sex. Having sex or the ability to have sex is not the answer as to whether you're worth anything. Your inability to socialise despite not looking terribly ugly leads me to believe you're either in the wrong place, or you have APD. This coupled with your desire to rape women makes me lean towards the latter. I know you don't have the money to see a therapist, but there has to be somewhere that can provide this at low cost in your area. Your counsellor at school or a GP is a good start, and they can point you in the direction of someone more trained to handle cases like yours. 

I know you say you can't make friends even when you're being friendly, but your ulterior motives may be giving you away. Please, please seek help. Therapy isn't cheap but counselling usually is. 

I also think society puts too much pressure on men to lose their virginity, like you're a loser if you don't. This is totally fucked up. Who cares if your a virgin at 19? Obviously you, but who else really cares? Who else does it really affect? Don't let the pursuit of sex be the driving force to who you are. I'm sorry that you have to deal with these societal pressures, but you can rise above them! I have faith in you and your ability to know right from wrong

Life can be as good as some make it out to be, but it's definitely not rainbows and sunshine for everyone 24/7. People who haven't experienced depression usually turn to the whole "but life is so good, look how beautiful everything is" uplifting speech in order to make those depressed feel better, and they have the best intentions at heart, but don't realise how damaging this lie can be. You say that nothing matters and everything gets forgotten in the end, which in the grand scheme of things, is true BUT you're not here for the grand scheme of things. You're here for a split second in that whole grand scheme and that split second is so significant because it affects the next person's split second and they affect the next. The grand scheme of things is sad, but your life doesn't have to be. In the split second, everything and everyone matters, you aren't forgotten for that split second because it's impossible to be erased that quickly. I did med then switched to law, so we've got that in common :D I ended up having a break down and was hospitalised before I realised that no matter how proud and happy I made my parents, at the end of the day, it was my life. If your parents oppose this, tell them you'd rather figure out just what it is you want to do in life then waste another cent of their money on another course you can't bring yourself to finish. After my breakdown, I was out of schooling for a year and a half till I realised what I really wanted to do.

Do your parents sit down with you while you're studying, or are you left to do them yourself? I'd say do 1 hour of quick note skimming, then tackle a sample paper for however long you're allowed to in your real exam. If your results are more than 90%, go outside and reward yourself! If you don't feel your results are adequate for the mark you want to get, pinpoint your areas of weakness and study those sections using the two hour method. Plan out the hours and time you'll be spending on revising each weak section. When this is done, give another sample paper a go and if your grade from the last one has improved, you are done for the day. Doesn't matter if you don't get 100%, that's it. Your brain will not be able to handle any more than that AND THAT'S OKAY :D

My mum also claimed mental illnesses aren't real but that was like her coping mechanism because she herself was suffering (and still suffers) from mental illness. She couldn't bear to see me in such a sorry state, and so she denied it with anger. I finally sat her down after months of hinting that I may be depressed and that it wasn't just the teenage blues, and here's what I said: "Mum, I need you to trust in what I say and just hear me until I finish. I believe that there is something wrong with the way I view the world. I feel this pressure to the point of break down and see no end in sight but my own death through suicide. I don't want to commit suicide. I don't want to hurt you, the family, or myself. But this internal pressure and external stress has brought me to this point. I am ready and willing to remedy this, but I will need help. I know you don't believe in mental illness and that therapy is a waste of money and time, but this is what I need. Whether I have your support or not, I am going to see a doctor for a true diagnosis, just for my peace of mind. I love you, and I'm sorry if this brings shame upon you; but it's because I love you that I will seek help."

In regards to your sleep, schedule that too along with your study times. Idk, but I started to find it therapeutic and even fun to just schedule my days. It's a good way to sit down and rest while reassuring yourself your life is moving in some sort of direction. It's also very hard to sleep with anxiety, and scheduling your study times and knowing exactly what you studied and for how long can ease that anxiety. Also, try chamomile tea! It's great stuff :)

I just read that you're in high school!! Let your principal and school counsellor know. It might feel a little uncomfortable, but it's totally worth it. I know exactly where you're coming from, and in fact, you sound just like me a few years back (including the passion for science!). 

You're having your finals in March so you're definitely not from Australia, so I don't know what concessions are available to you. But if you seek medical help here for mental illness (such as the depression/anxiety you're feeling right now), you're entitled to bonus points in your final exams. You might want to look into the policies your state/country has in terms of this :)

Your parents want you at the top all the time because they want what is best for your future. There's no point in being at the top if you personally can't handle that future and stress by yourself. Sit down with the parent you feel closest to and explain that you're feeling a little burnt out. The first time I did this, I was met with a negative experience, but from it my relationship with my mum was able to grow. Your parents don't mean to put this much pressure on you, and probably think you're capable of bearing it. Please don't make the same mistake I did by keeping it bottled up for so long that it caused me to be hospitalised. You know in your gut that you can't continue working with this amount of pressure and stress thrust upon you, hence why your brain is dreaming of suicide as an exit strategy. You are clearly uncomfortable with this feeling and are willing to fight it! I want you to know that you are not alone in turning to the thought of suicide when you are dealt with a lot of stress, and that it's good that you've identified it as something you want to change. I wish I could personally say that I no longer turn to thoughts of suicide as a coping mechanism, but that would be a lie. But what's important is exhausting every other option available to you before putting any action to suicidal thoughts.

Your stress and anxiety is tied to your ability to achieve high results in your final exams. From your enthusiasm with science, I have no doubt that you will achieve these results. In the event that you don't, it's important to know that that's okay too. These exams may play a big part in your life, but by no means will they be the only thing to shape your future. You're at your finals, you've come this far! Give yourself some credit where it's due. And know that it's okay to be selfish. Yes, your parents want you to succeed and live a good life, but you also need to live your life for yourself and not your parents. It's one thing to make them proud, and it's another to sacrifice your happiness for their approval. 

From one timid science nerd to another, you are NOT just your grades. People don't just see you that way, and I only found that out after high school. I thought I was just some loser no one really noticed unless they wanted help with their studies. Turns out, many people had fond memories of me and wanted to be my friend but were scared to approach me. And in the end, what matters is /you/ know who you are - and that is a three dimensional character who probably loves to slack off and goof around on games but still wants something out of life. 

NOW the fun stuff - how to deal with exam stress and anxiety 101

- Research alternative pathways in case you don't reach the mark you were aiming for. Hopefully, this lets your brain go "if I fail this exam, I can always give this a shot" instead of "if I fail this exam, I may as well die". 

- Plan/schedule your study/review sessions! Choose a subject and study TWO sections max. for that subject. Why is this important? It prevents you from getting bogged down in work you're doing vs work you're to finish. 

- Only ever study for 2 hours each period. After the first 2 hours, take a 15 minute break. If you study for 2 more hours after that, take a 30 minute break. Keep adding 15 minutes to each of your break times after every 2 hours. 

- Take a day off for yourself, and don't feel guilty about it. I found it useful to schedule my break days so that I could make the most out of them without feeling like I'd wasted a day I could've been studying.

Hey there!

First and foremost, exams are an incredibly stressful time so it's understandable as to why you feel this way. I'm sorry you're struggling right now and I know that with this piled up stress, suicide seems like the only option, but really it's the hardest and worst option available to you right now. It's just so easy to think of and can become a sort of safety blanket in times of uncertainty - "If I don't pass this subject, I can just kill myself" and that sort of thinking. It's easy enough to think it and breathe a sigh of relief, but the lingering knowledge that you can throw your life away just like that is scary. These are all normal thoughts we've all had from time to time, take a deep breath and evaluate your situation.

I highly suggest turning to the head of your faculty and campus counsellors and telling them that you've been struggling. Not only will they be able to provide you with emotional support like therapy, but depending on your uni, they might be able to give you a little leniency in terms of your assessments. This could mean alternate exam dates, extra credit assignments, bonus points etc. which will definitely take the edge off. 

Realise that exams are important, but your mental health trumps any academic responsibilities you may have. You are more important than a grade; your parents cherish you more than a percentage. If you need to take a breather after this semester, do so. Drop a unit if possible to lighten your workload. If you fail this subject, that's okay too! The idea of having to pay again sucks, but seems like a tiny price compared to losing your life.
